subject.title: fix(agents): repair double-escaped JSON strings in tool call argument…

question: Should OpenClaw accept a universal post-parse repair that may normalize valid literal escapes in code-like tool arguments, or should this remain restricted to independently proven malformed provider/stream representations?
rationale: The tests establish a useful fix for the reported corruption, but source evidence cannot determine the intended compatibility policy for valid literal escape content across all providers and tool payloads.

options.title: Use a bounded repair
options.body: Restrict normalization to an independently proven malformed stream/provider representation and retain exact valid argument bytes elsewhere.

options.title: Adopt generic normalization
options.body: Keep the all-provider wrapper, but explicitly approve the compatibility contract and add preservation coverage for the accepted cross-language and command cases.

options.title: Pause for root-cause instrumentation
options.body: Defer this heuristic until raw stream evidence identifies whether the corruption originates before or inside OpenClaw argument assembly.

recommendation.title: Use a bounded repair
recommendation.body: Restrict normalization to an independently proven malformed stream/provider representation and retain exact valid argument bytes elsewhere.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged adjacent repair established the current preserve-valid-arguments boundary in this subsystem.
